CPK Built
Release 1 blueprint · 16 Oct 2026
01 · Tech stack

Azure in Chennai, one TypeScript codebase

One codebase builds the web app and the Android app. The API and records run on Azure's basic and pay-per-use tiers in South India (Chennai), with backups in Central India (Pune). The data model shows every Release 1 table and the requirements it serves.

Technology stackData model
Figure 1 — CPK Built Release 1 application architecture, updated 16 Oct 2026 (simplified view of the stack below)
Technology stack
Apps people use
05
React Native + TypeScript
One codebase for the Android app and the web app.
Expo
Builds the Android APK and the web app; Expo Go for testing on phones.
Azure Static Web Apps (Free)
Hosts the web app for iPhone players and all staff.
Expo image picker and image manipulator
Capture or choose meal photos; shrink them and strip location data on the phone.
Expo SecureStore
Keeps Android sign-in tokens in the phone's secure storage.
Records and files
03
Azure SQL Database (Basic)
All Release 1 records, with row-level security; settings and tables are under Data model.
Azure Blob Storage
Movement reference media and meal photos; private, served through short-lived links; meal photos move to Cold after 90 days.
Repository layer
One data-access layer; records carry phone-generated IDs and timestamps.
Business rules
01
Azure Functions Flex Consumption
The TypeScript API; pay-per-use in the beta, about 2 s on the first request after idle.
Sign in and protection
06
Microsoft Entra External ID
Player and staff sign-in, verification and reset; free under 50,000 monthly users.
Emailed one-time code
The second step for staff sign-in.
App permissions
Role and branch rules, enforced by row-level security.
Key Vault + managed identities
Server credentials kept out of code; GitHub deploys sign in without stored passwords.
Azure VNet + service endpoint
Only the API's subnet reaches the database.
Existing chennaiparkour.fit DNS
The web app's address; no Azure DNS zone needed.
Build and operate
06
GitHub Free + Actions + Bicep
Version, test and deploy; production deploys by the App Admin after the Business Admin's go-ahead.
Expo EAS
Builds and signs the Android APK, shared through Google Drive.
Azure Monitor + Application Insights
Backend health, and alerts within five minutes; daily data cap.
Sentry (free)
App crash reports.
Blob protection
Soft delete for movement reference media.
Automated tests
Vitest, Playwright, Maestro, k6 and axe in GitHub Actions (epic E15).
Not neededSupabase, Firestore, MSG91, FastAPI, a separate sync platform, an Azure DNS zone or an App Service plan.
Data model
40 tables in Azure SQL for Release 1, in six domains. Each table lists the user stories and non-functional requirements it serves; each feature in 03 lists its tables.

Tables and relations
Figure 2 — Release 1 data model by domain; arrows point from the tables that refer to another domain’s tables. Every domain also links to person.

Every table has id (a GUID, generated on the phone for logged sets so a retry never duplicates), created_at and updated_at in UTC. Branch-scoped tables also carry franchise_id and branch_id, and franchise-scoped tables carry franchise_id; row-level security filters on them. Library tables are shared across the network.

03 · Epics, features and user stories

15 epics, every story traced

Every feature has a permanent ID: E01-F06 is epic 01, feature 06. Functional stories add US (E01-F06-US01); non-functional requirements add NFR (E01-F08-NFR01). Each feature shows its Release 1 build sequence; the full order is in 04 · Project plan. Release 1 builds 33 features through 121 user stories, held to 26 non-functional requirements.

Vocabulary, in the Chennai Parkour spirit of play: the member is the Player, the coach is the Coach, and the workout plan is the Gameplan.

Epic numbers follow C:\CPK_Built as built on 6 Sep 2026 (question 1), with three changes to confirm (question 2): E01 merges platform foundation and operations (EPIC-01 and EPIC-14), E14 is special programmes (was EPIC-15) and E15 automated testing is new. E01-F14 data import, E09-F05 nutrition plan and meal log, E12-F05 coach notes and the non-functional groups E01-F08 to E01-F13 are also new; E02-F06 movement edit approval is deferred to R2. Features outside Release 1 get their stories when scheduled. IDs are permanent from this baseline: a removed item's ID is retired, never reused. Requirements follow the latest executive review, including WhatsApp group messages (E13-F01-US03).

Roles and RACI
Release 1 roles, the roles that come later, and who does what. R does the work, A is accountable, and I gets a notification; no Release 1 workflow needs a C.

E01-F10-NFR01AvailabilityTarget 99.9% monthly API uptime and 99.8% crash-free mobile sessions.Target held on SLA-backed services, without zone redundancy at this budget; crash-free sessions tracked in Sentry.E15-F01-US05R1

04 · Project plan

From accounts to the 16 Nov start

Accounts first, then the 33 Release 1 features in sequence from 15 Oct to 6 Nov. The beta goes live on Monday 9 Nov, after Deepavali and a week before the 12-week programme starts on 16 Nov.

How to startWorkbook fixesPlan to launchBuild orderRisksGo/no-goAfter Release 1

Risks and mitigations
RiskEffectMitigation
Added scope: sign-off, movement editing and the nutrition logThe build runs to 3 Nov with little slackPush reminders moved after the beta; the meal review (E09-F05-US06) lands by 23 Nov
Meal photo privacyThe wrong person sees a player's photosNeed-to-know access, audited staff views and permission tests (E01-F11-NFR07, E15-F05-US01)
Nutritionist capacity35 nutrition plans needed before 16 NovPlan copying (E09-F05-US02); plans entered during the 10–13 Nov experience sessions
About 2 s on the first request after idleThe app feels slow at the start of a batchTell testers; a free uptime check pinging the API in gym hours can reduce it; the always-ready instance (~₹530 a month) removes it
No offline modeLogging fails on weak signal; ECR is on the 2nd floorGym Wi-Fi for players; a failed save stays marked with a retry (E09-F01-US04)
AI-written code with a hidden flaw, and no outside reviewerData leak or wrong permissionsPermission matrix, diff checks, ChatGPT review and a restore drill (E15-F05)

Stage-to-level mapping unclearLevel awards (E02-F05) can't be computedSettle question 4 before R1 seq 28

Health declaration questions not suppliedActivation is blockedQuestions by 23 Oct (question 5)

APK signing key lostUpdates won't install over the old appExpo stores the key; never let it be regenerated
Your available hoursApprovals and testing pile upPlan around the hours you confirm (question 11)

  • Privacy policy and account-deletion page live on chennaiparkour.fit
  • Real coaches and players invited; week-1 gameplans and the movement library published
  • Nutritionist account set up and nutrition plans entered for every beta player

Monthly total~₹650~₹1,375~₹1,905 with always-ready
One-time₹0—~₹2,420 for Google Play ($25)

The ceiling — $25 is about ₹2,420 at ₹96.8 per dollar. A private endpoint (~₹755) or the S0 database tier (~₹950) fits only if you skip both the always-ready instance and GitHub Team.

Media — Movement reference photos and videos cost a few rupees a month in storage, and viewing them stays within Azure's 100 GB of free monthly data transfer at beta scale.

Meal photos — About ₹10–20 a month at beta scale (35 players, about 6 photos a day at about 250 KB). A lifecycle rule moves photos to Cold after 90 days; at 500 players over a year that cuts storage from about ₹550 to about ₹225 a month, plus small per-photo tier-change charges.

Basis — List prices checked 12–16 Oct 2026; GST (18%) excluded; confirm Azure in the pricing calculator in INR before approval.

Not counted — Your Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions, Razorpay fees (no payments in Release 1), and any domain-email plan the business enrolment needs.
